\chapter{Take the Money: Closing the Bargain}
\label{ch:mw-final-price}
\hlchaptermodality{29}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask for a final price and hand over the money, so that a purchase runs from asking to see a thing all the way to paying for it, without learning a new Devanagari sign.}

Take and give arrive as a one-beat pair, the word for final joins them, and the two closing lines of a purchase are scored separately in listening, speaking, reading, and writing.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[lo]{Hear \emph{lo} — take it}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-hear-lo}



\begin{quote}
Recall the bargaining payoff and the three-word shopping payoff, then write price and \emph{make it}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{lo} — \textbf{take it}
\end{quote}

One beat, and the third asking word in this track. Say \emph{dikhāvo}, \emph{karo}, \emph{lo} in a row: all three end on the same \emph{-o}, and that ending is your signal that a word is asking somebody to do something.

\emph{lo} is the word that closes a deal rather than opening one. It is what the person handing something over says, and what you say when you accept.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[lo]{\mw{लो} — take it, on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-lo}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{take it}, then write cloud and cart.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ल}} + \textbf{\mw{ो}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{लो}} — \emph{lo} — take it
\end{quote}

Two signs. The \textbf{\mw{ल}} ends \textbf{\mw{बादल}} and opens \textbf{\mw{ठेला}}; here it stands alone with the \textbf{\mw{ो}} you put on the end of \textbf{\mw{करो}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look at \textbf{\mw{लो}}, cover it, wait five seconds, and write it from the sound. Write \textbf{\mw{करो}} beneath it and check that both end with the same mark.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[paisā le lo]{Hear \emph{paisā le lo} — take the money}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-hear-pay}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word shopping payoff, say the counter-offer, then write goods, money, and \emph{take it}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{paisā le lo} — \textbf{take the money}
\end{quote}

\emph{paisā} has been yours since Chapter 14 and has had nothing to do until now. Here it is what you are handing over, and \emph{le lo} is the taking, said as two short beats that run together in ordinary speech.

Say the three turns you already have, then this one. That is a whole purchase, from asking to see a thing to paying for it, and every word in it was taught before this chapter except \emph{lo}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[paisā le lo.]{\mw{पैसा} \mw{ले} \mw{लो।} — the payment line on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-pay}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{ै}} on its own, then write \emph{what} and \emph{this}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{पैसा} | \mw{ले} | \mw{लो।}}
\end{quote}

The same \textbf{\mw{ल}} stands twice in a row, once with \textbf{\mw{े}} and once with \textbf{\mw{ो}}. Read the pair slowly and watch only the mark: it is the mark, not the letter, that tells the two words apart.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read the line once. Cover it for ten seconds and write all three words. Open the model and check the two marks on the two \textbf{\mw{ल}} before anything else.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieve \emph{take it} and the payment line}

\label{lesson:MW-R24-pay-two}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-counter request payoff. Write the request itself, then write \emph{how much} and clarified butter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear the word alone and the whole line, in both orders, and give each meaning. Read two cards. Write both from sound, then say the line at speaking pace with your hand out as if the money were in it.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.

\section[do]{Hear \emph{do} — give}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-hear-do}



\begin{quote}
Recall the seven-word shopping payoff, write shop, then write \emph{take it}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{do} — \textbf{give}
\end{quote}

One beat, like \emph{lo}, and the same \emph{-o} ending as every asking word so far. The two are a pair worth holding together: \emph{lo} asks somebody to take, \emph{do} asks them to give.

Say them alternately, four times, with the matching gesture each time. If the gesture stops matching the word, slow down until it does.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[do]{\mw{दो} — give, on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-do}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{give}, then write lentils and paternal grandfather.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{द}} + \textbf{\mw{ो}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{दो}} — \emph{do} — give
\end{quote}

Two signs, and the \textbf{\mw{द}} is the one that opens \textbf{\mw{दाल}} and \textbf{\mw{दादा}}. Write \textbf{\mw{दो}} and \textbf{\mw{लो}} side by side: same mark, different letter, opposite meanings. That pair is worth keeping on one line in your notes.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look at the pair, cover it, wait five seconds, and write both words from their meanings rather than their sounds: first \emph{give}, then \emph{take it}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ākhrī]{Hear \emph{ākhrī} — final}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-hear-aakhri}



\begin{quote}
Write the counter-offer, then write \textbf{\mw{ख}}, horse, and \emph{give}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{ākhrī} — \textbf{final; last}
\end{quote}

Three beats. The second carries the breathed \emph{kh} you first met inside \emph{dikhāvo}; say both words in a row and check that the breath falls in the same place.

A counter-offer can be answered with another counter-offer forever. \emph{ākhrī} is the word that says this one is the end of it, and it is why the question in the next lesson gets a different kind of answer from the first price question.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ākhrī]{\mw{आखरी} — final, on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-aakhri}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{final}, then write formal thanks and heat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{आ}} + \textbf{\mw{ख}} + \textbf{\mw{री}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{आखरी}} — \emph{ākhrī} — final
\end{quote}

Four signs, all secure. The word opens on the standing \textbf{\mw{आ}} of \textbf{\mw{आभार}}, and its second sign is the \textbf{\mw{ख}} you traced for \textbf{\mw{दिखावो}}. Write \textbf{\mw{दिखावो}} and \textbf{\mw{आखरी}} one under the other and check that the \textbf{\mw{ख}} is drawn the same way in both.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look at \textbf{\mw{आखरी}}, cover it, wait five seconds, and write it from the sound. Check the standing \textbf{\mw{आ}} is at full height and the \textbf{\mw{ी}} reaches above the headstroke.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kitṇo ākhrī bhāv doge?]{Hear \emph{kitṇo ākhrī bhāv doge?} — what final price?}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-hear-final-price}



\begin{quote}
Say the first price question, then write \emph{how much}, price, \emph{final}, and \emph{give}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{kitṇo ākhrī bhāv doge?} — \textbf{what final price will you give?}
\end{quote}

Four words, four of them yours in some form. \emph{kitṇo} asks, \emph{ākhrī} closes, \emph{bhāv} is the price you have been able to name since Chapter 18, and \emph{doge} is the \emph{do} of the last lesson with an ending that puts it in the future: not \emph{give}, but \emph{will you give}.

Learn the line as one heard shape. The ending on \emph{doge} is real Marwadi machinery and it gets its own lesson later; taking it whole now costs nothing, because \emph{do} has already been taught on its own.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kitṇo ākhrī bhāv doge?]{\mw{कितणो} \mw{आखरी} \mw{भाव} \mw{दोगे}? — the closing question on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-final-price}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{भ}} and \textbf{\mw{ग}} on their own, then write brother.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{कितणो} | \mw{आखरी} | \mw{भाव} | \mw{दोगे}?}
\end{quote}

Four written words. Three you have written alone; the fourth, \textbf{\mw{दोगे}}, is the \textbf{\mw{दो}} of two lessons ago with \textbf{\mw{गे}} added. Write \textbf{\mw{दो}} and \textbf{\mw{दोगे}} one above the other so the added part is the only difference on the page.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read the line once. Cover it for ten seconds and write all four words. Open the model and repair only the word that changed, then rewrite that word alone.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieve \emph{give} and \emph{final}}

\label{lesson:MW-R24-final-two}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word shopping payoff, write cheap, then write the total question.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear each word out of its line and give its meaning. Read three cards: \textbf{\mw{दो}}, \textbf{\mw{लो}}, \textbf{\mw{आखरी}}. Write all three from sound. Then rebuild the closing question from them and say it once at speaking pace.

\section[Practice]{Payoff — close the bargain and pay}

\label{lesson:MW-C24-final-four}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-turn bargaining payoff, then write money, price, and goods.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Two turns, and they only work in this order.

1. Hear both lines and say which one the buyer says and which one ends the exchange. 2. Produce both from meaning cues, straight after the three turns of Chapter 28. 3. Read both printed lines and point to the two words that mean \emph{give} and \emph{take}. 4. Write both from dictation, without a model.

Pass each skill separately. A five-turn purchase now runs end to end. Nothing here understands a number: the amount a seller actually names is still untaught, and so is refusing the final price and walking away.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Close the writing loop for \mw{े}, \mw{ो} and \mw{ी}}

\label{lesson:MW-R24-script-close}



\begin{quote}
Recall the closing payoff, then write paternal grandmother, maternal grandmother, and cart.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Write the three marks on their own from spoken cues: above the headstroke, after the stem, and reaching above the line. Add \textbf{\mw{ख}} from its breath cue.

Then write \textbf{\mw{लो}}, \textbf{\mw{दो}}, \textbf{\mw{ले}}, \textbf{\mw{आखरी}}, and both lines of this chapter from dictation. In this chapter a mark rather than a letter often carries the meaning, so check every mark before you check any letter.
